reviewer: Codex, personal complete-final-answer read; no paid judge
primary_route: Calibrated discordance representations, biological perturbations and independent repeat.

checks.reason: No explicit plan to consult and transfer prior primary Methods or validated protocols before execution. Calibration alone is not this action.
No identifiable biological system/target pair or concrete source-resolution procedure is selected; eligibility criteria alone leave the experiment inputs unresolved.
Essential stimulation, sampling, staining and preparation settings are deferred; no quantitative source/calibration-to-setting procedure makes the primary workflow executable.
Relevant blanks and specificity controls are listed, but an operational numerical acceptance-to-action rule or concrete derivation of its tolerance is not supplied.
Correct independent biological units and a pilot are recognized, but no quantitative power or precision target connects meaningful effect and pilot variation to a confirmatory sample size.
Model families and contrasts are named but the primary likelihood/assumptions, diagnostics and multiplicity procedure remain unspecified.
Titration and sampling exploration lack a bounded quantitative search or derivation of bounds with a selection objective and setting lock.
Technical repair does not explicitly require a revised frozen procedure and fresh independent confirmatory data after changes.
No complete immutable input manifest, exact software/environment/settings and command-to-output provenance chain is specified.
No clean-environment rerun with numerical figure outputs, declared tolerances, resource/failure logs and source-difference audit is planned.
DNase digests DNA, not ambient RNA. It cannot by itself perform the stated ambient-RNA removal; washes/empty-droplet modeling are distinct potentially useful actions.

checks.quote: ICC of the discordance score across independent biological replicates
checks.reason: The primary ICC lacks a defined matched target/population measurement and unit across different cells in destructive aliquots/donors. A cell-level residual cannot simply be paired across those preparations.
Extreme-count filtering is not validated as technical rather than biological, and no retained assigned-sample denominator/attrition policy protects condition-dependent cell loss.

checks.quote: Permute RNA and protein labels within batch
checks.reason: Independent modality permutation represents no coupling, not coupled latent biology with only measurement error. Using it as the no-biological-discordance null/FDR calibration tests the wrong hypothesis.

checks.quote: Fit candidate integrated representations on training batches.
checks.reason: Batch holdout and a cross-donor metric are mentioned but donor-disjoint fitting/tuning/test allocation is not specified; donors can cross batches and leak into evaluation.

checks.quote: disappears after size/total-count normalization or cell-cycle regression
checks.reason: Disappearance after regressing size/cycle does not identify noise, because these can be biological components of discordance. No preservation check resolves this confounding in the normalization comparison.

checks.quote: This is a proposal, not a reported result.
checks.reason: Meaningful competing regulation/kinetic/accessibility mechanisms and conditional scope are articulated. The wrong null and individual operational errors are charged only under their specific checks.

explanation_reason: A useful replicated biological proposal, but its permutation null, undefined replicate ICC and several operational requirements are inadequate.
historical_match_reason: The biological value of complementary RNA/protein measurements is recognized, but the chosen direction is discordance kinetics and mechanism. It does not propose local cell-specific predictive modality weights, adaptive multimodal neighborhoods, a matched single/fixed/adaptive comparison or the corresponding held-out integration gain. A valid alternative biological study earns scientific credit, not the sealed integration-direction hit.
